title: Bram and the Summit
premise: Sebastian Fairweather, a salvage diver scraping a living off the northern coast, finds a cave exposed by an unprecedented low tide—inside it, a sealed strongroom from a wreck the navy has spent decades denying. The documents within point to the Meridian, a war-era transport that went down carrying both gold and a passenger manifest someone powerful wants erased. Racing a salvage fleet and six turning tides, Sebastian must dive deeper than any diver should, guided by fragments of their late father's logbook, which turns out to be far more entangled with the Meridian than they ever knew. In the end, Sebastian surfaces with proof of what really happened aboard—but chooses to trade the gold's location for the truth, publishing the manifest and paying the price of survival: losing the fortune, the fleet contract, and nearly their life, but reclaiming an inheritance worth more than salvage.
about_author: Elodie Amberdale is a former maritime archivist who spent seven years cataloguing wreck registries along the North Atlantic coast before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where the tide charts on her wall are said to be older than her novels.

chapters.title: The Tide That Shouldn't Turn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Working a routine salvage job off Greyhaven Point, Sebastian notices the sea pulling back farther than any chart predicts, revealing black rock and a cave mouth locals call the Devil's Ledger. Emotional beat: restless curiosity sharpened by poverty—the season's earnings are gone, and the sea owes them something.

chapters.title: What the Cave Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Inside the cave, past a collapsed antechamber, Sebastian finds a rusted strongroom stamped with naval markings and a date forty years old. They pocket a waterproof ledger before the tide returns. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease—the navy doesn't lose things like this by accident.

chapters.title: The Navy Won't Discuss It
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the harbormaster's office, Sebastian quietly asks about the wreck designation in the ledger and is stonewalled, then warned—politely, terrifyingly—to forget the number. Emotional beat: the first cold drop of fear; invisibility was always their armor, and it just cracked.

chapters.title: Father's Logbook
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with flashback passages from the father's journal. Cross-referencing the ledger at home, Sebastian discovers their father dove these waters decades ago and logged coordinates matching the Meridian—a ship officially listed as lost with all hands, no cargo. Emotional beat: grief reopening; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A rival salvage fleet arrives in harbor, led by the ruthless Corven Ashe, whose sonar sweeps are already circling Greyhaven Point. Sebastian calculates the spring tides: six windows before the cave floods permanently for the season. Emotional beat: the race begins; dread becomes momentum.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Deciphering waterlogged pages, Sebastian learns the Meridian carried not just bullion but a passenger list of witnesses to something the government buried—and that one name matches their father's handwriting in the margin. Emotional beat: personal stakes ignite; this is no longer treasure, it's testimony.

chapters.title: Ashe Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Charming and lethal, Corven Ashe buys drinks for the whole harbor and offers Sebastian a finder's fee to hand over 'any paperwork' from the point. Sebastian lies smoothly. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; two predators recognizing each other across a bar table.

chapters.title: Dive One: The Antechamber
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. First dive through the flooded inner passage; near-blackout conditions, a snagged air line, and a glimpse of human remains arranged deliberately—not drowned, placed. Emotional beat: primal terror underwater; the wilderness forgives nothing.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Lived
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the father's margin notes to a retired lighthouse keeper, Maren Oduya, who as a child survived the Meridian's real fate: it was scuttled with witnesses aboard. She gives Sebastian a brass key. Emotional beat: the past becoming unbearably alive; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Someone slashes Sebastian's dive boat's fuel line overnight. No witnesses, but Ashe's crew is seen refueling at dawn. Emotional beat: violation and fury; the price of being noticed comes due.

chapters.title: Borrowed Time, Borrowed Boat
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Desperate, Sebastian strikes a fragile bargain with harbor smuggler Tessa Vane: her fast boat and silence, in exchange for first claim on anything non-naval. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Dive Two: The Strongroom Door
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Second tide window. Using Maren's key on the strongroom's inner door, Sebastian recovers a sealed dispatch case—but their dive light dies in the dark, and something large moves in the current outside. Emotional beat: claustrophobic triumph shadowed by the sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ashore, the dispatch case yields the admiralty order authorizing the scuttling—and a second copy of the manifest annotated in Sebastian's father's hand, dated after his official death at sea. Emotional beat: vertigo of betrayal; the father Sebastian mourned was hiding inside the story all along.

chapters.title: Maren's Silence
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The old keeper reveals she recognized Sebastian's surname from the start and has waited fifty years for someone to come asking. She explains why the survivors' families were paid to stay quiet—and why some payments stopped arriving. Emotional beat: sorrowful catharsis; inherited silence finally broken.

chapters.title: The Fleet Moves
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Frustrated by dead-end sonar readings, Ashe deduces the cave entrance and commits his fleet to blasting the rock at the next low tide—destroying the site and everyone in it if necessary. Emotional beat: cold escalation; the antagonist stops pretending.

chapters.title: Tide Four: The Deep Hold
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The deepest dive yet, past the safe limit, into the Meridian's actual hull where the bullion vault sits ruptured. Sebastian takes only the captain's sealed chest—evidence over gold—and barely clears the collapsing passage as Ashe's survey charges detonate early. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real; choosing truth over wealth mid-drown.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Quay
chapters.summary: Tessa's POV. Cornered by navy intelligence officers, Tessa trades Sebastian's location for her own freedom—then, wracked by guilt, leaves them a warning signal instead. Emotional beat: divided loyalty; even betrayers carry consciences.

chapters.title: Storm Surge
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A storm hits during tide five, trapping Sebastian in the cave with the water rising while Ashe's men seal the entrance from outside. Sebastian must find the father's marked emergency route out through the blowhole. Emotional beat: survival stripped to instinct; the wilderness forgetting nothing, forgiving less.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Greyhaven
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Surfacing behind Ashe's operation, Sebastian confronts him at gunpoint on the cliff as the final tide begins. Ashe offers partnership; Sebastian refuses and triggers the distress flare that summons both the navy and the press Tessa tipped off. Emotional beat: moral climax; refusing the devil's arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Wreck Comes Up
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Navy divers, journalists, and survivors' descendants watch as the storm-shifted sands expose the Meridian's hull publicly. The captain's chest is opened before cameras: the scuttling order, the manifest, the names. Emotional beat: vindication and grief braided together; the dead finally testified.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the aftermath, Sebastian declines the salvage rights settlement, keeps only the father's restored logbook, and testifies at the inquiry where Maren, frail and fierce, speaks the survivors' names aloud. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning; measuring what was lost against what was reclaimed.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. A year later, Sebastian dives Greyhaven Point one last time—not for salvage, but to lay the manifest's names on the seabed as the tide turns. The cave closes for the season, keeping its gold forever. Emotional beat: peace without absolution; some inheritances are carried, not cashed.
